description: Team Role & Project Overview: Participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge (Abandoned but not Forgotten), our team bridges complex space history and young minds. We transform raw technical data into an engaging, story-driven digital experience that brings dormant rovers and landers on the Moon and Mars back to life. By blending factual accuracy with creative storytelling, we inspire the next generation to connect with humanity’s robotic pioneers and their science.
summary:
**After The Signal** is an interactive educational platform that brings the stories of abandoned, inactive, and retired space exploration equipment to life.

The platform focuses on missions and equipment deployed on the Moon and Mars, allowing users to explore their history, scientific discoveries, mission milestones, and lasting contributions to space exploration.

Through immersive storytelling, interactive mission timelines, multilingual support, customizable content modes, and an AI-powered assistant, After The Signal transforms complex space exploration information into an engaging and accessible learning experience.

Our mission is to preserve the stories behind every signal sent from beyond Earth, reminding users that even when a mission ends, its discoveries continue to shape our understanding of the universe.
details:
After The Signal — Project Details

Project Overview

After The Signal is an interactive web platform dedicated to documenting and exploring the stories of space exploration equipment whose missions have ended, become inactive, or lost communication.

It currently focuses on equipment and missions associated with the Moon and Mars, presenting their historical background, scientific achievements, mission journeys, and lasting impact.

Problem Statement

Space exploration has produced an enormous amount of valuable scientific and historical information. However, stories about retired or inactive exploration equipment are often scattered across different sources and presented in ways that may be difficult for general audiences to explore.

As a result, the achievements of these missions can become overlooked once communication ends or their operational life comes to a close.

Our Solution

After The Signal provides a centralized and interactive experience that organizes these stories into accessible digital archives.

Users can explore space equipment by location, discover detailed mission stories, follow chronological mission timelines, and interact with an AI-powered assistant to learn more about space exploration.

Key Features

  • Interactive Exploration: Browse space exploration equipment from the Moon and Mars.
  • Detailed Artifact Stories: Discover each mission's background, scientific discoveries, achievements, and legacy.
  • Mission Timeline: Explore important events throughout each mission's operational history.
  • AI-Powered Assistant: Ask questions about space exploration and receive AI-generated responses.
  • Multilingual Experience: Support for English, Arabic, Spanish, and French.
  • Customizable Reading Modes: Choose between Cadet, All, and Telemetry content modes.
  • Theme Customization: Switch between dark and light visual themes.
  • Responsive Design: Access the platform across different screen sizes.

Target Audience

  • Students and educational communities.
  • Space and astronomy enthusiasts.
  • People interested in science, technology, and space exploration.
  • Anyone curious about the history and achievements of space missions.

Technology Stack

Frontend

  • Angular 22
  • TypeScript
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Angular Signals
  • RxJS
  • Angular Router
  • Server-Side Rendering (SSR)
  • Hydration

Backend

  • ASP.NET Core Web API
  • RESTful API architecture
  • AI Assistant integration

Future Development

  • Expand the archive with more space missions and exploration equipment.
  • Complete the integration of all equipment data with the backend database.
  • Improve AI responses using trusted scientific sources and mission-specific information.
  • Add richer visual storytelling and interactive mission experiences.
  • Introduce additional destinations beyond the Moon and Mars.

Project Vision

Our vision is to preserve the scientific and historical legacy of space exploration by transforming forgotten or inactive missions into accessible, engaging, and educational digital stories.

Because a mission may end, but its story doesn't have to.
